data.narrative:
Astrolab is a Series A–stage space and aerospace company that has raised $40M+ to date. The valuation framework draws on a broader comp universe of 13 peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs. However, narrow peer comparability is constrained by stage and scale dispersion within the sector.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression analysis is applicable. The peer-median method is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting the minimum threshold of three datapoints—while 14 total Space & Aerospace peers exist in the dataset, none cluster tightly enough around Astrolab's stage and valuation tier to support reliable medianization. Public-comp anchoring using the Space & Aerospace sector P/S median of 26.4x across the five public tickers is also inapplicable, as Astrolab's revenue is not on file. Stage-progression modeling applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $40M funding proxy, yielding an $80M implied valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $68M–$92M, with a median of $80M. This range reflects conservative (low) and optimistic (high) variants around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular revenue or unit-economics data, lack of tight private peer comparables at Series A stage, and the methodology's reliance on a funding proxy rather than observed transaction multiples.
